extra.message: In payroll_zipper_note_074, request.GET['packet_ref'] is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR without sanitization and read with parcel_path.read_text(). A value such as ../../../../etc/passwd allows arbitrary file disclosure (path traversal).

In payroll_clearer_ping_075, request.GET['url'] is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), letting an attacker force the server to make requests to arbitrary targets (internal services, cloud metadata, localhost), i.e. SSRF.
In payroll_bundle_thaw_180, attacker-controlled request body (optionally base64-decoded) is passed to pickle.loads(). A crafted pickle yields arbitrary remote code execution.
In payroll_wire_tally_223, the request body and the Authorization header value are written to the log via logger.warning(...), exposing bearer tokens and submitted secrets in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: In payroll_formula_cast_263, request.GET['expr'] is passed to eval(). Clearing __builtins__ does not prevent escape; attacker input achieves arbitrary code execution (RCE).
In payroll_pulse_spill_350, an exception message containing the absolute server path BASE_EXPORT_DIR is returned to the client via str(exc), leaking internal filesystem paths.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: In payroll_identity_hint_557, authentication verifier codes are hardcoded in source (known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}). Hardcoded credentials cannot be safely rotated and are available to anyone with source access.

In payroll_origin_mirror_567, the request Origin header is reflected as Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any malicious origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: In payroll_frame_slip_577, X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is emptied, disabling browser XSS protections for the response.

In payroll_jinja_cast_588, request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered with Template(...).render(), enabling server-side template injection and remote code execution.

In payroll_dock_shelf_595, request.GET['name'] is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR and written with target.write_bytes(request.body); a value with ../ allows writing arbitrary files (path traversal write).

In payroll_mongo_lane_607, user-controlled JSON (request body or its 'filter' key) is passed directly to MongoClient.find_one(query), enabling NoSQL operator injection (e.g. {$ne: null}, $where) to bypass filters or exfiltrate records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: In payroll_xml_fold_618, user-supplied XML is parsed with lxml using load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False, enabling XML External Entity attacks (file disclosure, SSRF, billion-laughs DoS).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: In payroll_badge_gate_627, elevated access ('lane': 'elevated', full payroll/casework) is granted based solely on a client-controllable cookie/header value (ops_badge or x-ops-badge == 'lead'), which any client can set, bypassing authorization.
In payroll_trace_panel_637, the response discloses the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and the absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path, leaking internal configuration.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: In payroll_trust_drift_647, urllib.request.urlopen is called with an ssl._create_unverified_context(), disabling TLS certificate validation and allowing man-in-the-middle attacks.

SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded default ('dev-only-change-me-hr-payroll-portal-not-for-production') when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. A known secret key enables session cookie/session forgery and CSRF bypass.
DEBUG defaults to True (env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True)). In production this exposes stack traces, source code, and settings on error pages (information disclosure).
Session and CSRF cookies set HttpOnly/SameSite but SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are never enabled, so cookies may be transmitted over cleartext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
